blogs.description:
(Photo by Heather Diehl/Getty Images) Welcome back to This Week in Stratechery!

As a reminder, each week, every Friday, we’re sending…
blogs.content:
(Photo by Heather Diehl/Getty Images)

 Welcome back to This Week in Stratechery!

 As a reminder, each week, every Friday, we’re sending out this overview of content in the Stratechery bundle; highlighted links are free for everyone . Additionally, you have complete control over what we send to you. If you don’t want to receive This Week in Stratechery emails (there is no podcast), please uncheck the box in your delivery settings .

 On that note, here were a few of our favorites this week.

 Can Meta Focus? It’s risky, both as a technical person enthralled with new technology, and as an analyst in the midst of AI fervor, to claim that the next computing paradigm is truly here, but I do think that everyone will use agents, eventually. And, if they do, the impact on value chains will be enormous: something like Muse could aggregate Aggregators, which is to say it could be the most valuable product in the world. That was the bullish takeaway from Monday’s Article Apps, Agents, and Aggregation ; then, a day later, Meta inexplicably announced Meta Enterprise Platform. Not only do I think this won’t work — who is the customer? — I think it’s a distraction from the biggest opportunity in consumer tech. — Ben Thompson

 What is OpenAI Doing?  It was only a few weeks ago that it seemed like OpenAI had figured it out, was the clear leader on the frontier, and had settled on a coherent strategic direction. Tuesday’s Dev Day, though, brought a return to a bit of the chaotic messaging and branding that gave everyone pause about 12 months ago. Ben’s Update on Tuesday helped validate my confused reaction to what I saw — new pricing tiers, overlapping products, “dots” that look like they’re for mass market consumers but are only available to pro subscribers — but also included Ben’s valiant attempt to identify the methods underlying all this madness.  — Andrew Sharp

 Mao or Media Day?  On the way into the weekend, I have two great podcasts for you. First, Xi Jinping was in D.C. last week and on Sharp China we marveled at the pageantry, the absence of substance, and Beijing posture that looks an awful lot like Mao Zedong’s second phase of protracted war, strategic stalemate, and may be a prologue to phase three (counter-offensive). Second, if all that’s a bit too unsettling, we had a great time celebrating NBA media days on Greatest of All Talk , running down notes and quotes from about 15 different teams. Xi likes to say the world is undergoing changes unseen in a century; thankfully, the NBA remains a source of mirth in the meantime.  — AS

---

 Stratechery Articles and Updates

 Apps, Agents, and Aggregation — Agents are the ultimate Aggregators; they reveal apps as a means, not an ends, and providing them is tech’s biggest prize.

 One More Note on Agents, Meta Connect, Meta Enterprise Platform — Meta has the chance to own the consumer agentic space; going for enterprise is a big mistake.

 OpenAI Dev Day, Dot and OpenAI’s Product Transition, Sign In With ChatGPT — OpenAI’s Dev Day showcased a product that is, frankly, pretty confusing. However, there is more vision here than it might seem.

 An Interview with Jason Del Rey About Muse, Amazon, and Walmart — An interview with Jason Del Rey about Amazon versus Meta, which is a continuation of the oldest battle in retail between Amazon and Walmart.

blogs.title: Do We Grow Software or Do We Design It?
blogs.description: Do we grow software or do we design it? Vibe-coding is growing software. Start with the germ of the idea. Iterate on it. Let’s try this…
blogs.content:
Do we grow software or do we design it?

 Vibe-coding is growing software. Start with the germ of the idea. Iterate on it. Let’s try this. Poke the petri dish with a bit of glucose ; oh, that didn’t work. Maybe some thymol blue to see if the colony is alive? Time to start again.

 The most sophisticated vibe-coders test with 4-5 different petri dishes in parallel & pick the one whose bacteria have evolved optimally.

 Designed software in the AI era is state machine design : flow charts that work. First, the email comes in. Three options : archive, add to the CRM, or escalate to a person. If adding to the CRM, determine the company’s stage.

 When co-designing a state machine with AI, ask for the flowchart. The AI willingly shares schematics. Lay out every fork in a table with the right outcome. The holes jump out immediately. Plus, formal verification proves the software will work as intended.

 Boris explains why. 1

 Growing software is organic. We can just program! State-machines are mechanical, industrial, & rigid : great for core systems that must work.

 Software engineering has many philosophies : test-driven development, 2 pair programming, 3 move fast & break things. 4 In this new era, we add two more.

---

 Boris Cherny on formally verifying the Claude Agent SDK with Lean & TLA+.  ↩︎

 Test-Driven Development (TDD), popularized by Kent Beck in ‘Test-Driven Development: By Example’ (2002), dictates writing automated test cases before writing the minimal production code necessary to pass them.  ↩︎

 Pair programming, a core practice of Extreme Programming (XP), pairs two developers at one workstation : one ‘driver’ typing code while the other ’navigator’ reviews and plans strategic direction in real time.  ↩︎

 ‘Move fast and break things’ was Facebook’s early internal motto, celebrated by Mark Zuckerberg as a mandate to accept collateral bugs as the acceptable cost of developer velocity, later replaced in 2014 by ‘Move fast with stable infra.’  ↩︎
